newsitem.title: USA: Motorola sees gradual DRAM phase-out.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees gradual DRAM phase-out.

text.p: Motorola Inc, which will take a second-quarter pretax charge of $170 million to exit the dynamic random access memory (DRAM) market, said Tuesday it will phase-out production in stages by mid-2000.
In the first stage, Motorola expects to end 16-megabit DRAM production at a Japanese joint-venture plant with Toshiba Corp by the end of this year, a spokesman said.
Motorola's production of 64-megabit DRAM at a Siemens AG joint venture plant now under construction in Virginia is expected to end in mid-2000.
Motorola is moving out of DRAM to focus on faster memory products used in higher-speed computers, such as flash static random access memory products.
"We're the world leader in higher performance, fast-static random access memory," Ken Phillips, director of communications for Motorola's Semiconductor Product Sector, told Reuters.
While the new generations of higher speed computers also use DRAM, this market is more competitive and fragmented with suppliers, Phillips said.
Motorola declined to comment on the current financial conditions of its DRAM business. But another company spokesman said on a conference call today that the DRAM segment was not profitable in 1996.
Motorola plans to use its half of the White Oak Semiconductor joint venture plant, being built with Siemens, to make fast-static RAM products.
The electronics and technology giant plans to shift its share of output at the Toshiba venture into local products for computers.
Phillips said the shift out of DRAM into other computer memory and logic products reflects Motorola's strategy to organize its businesses based on market focus as opposed to product groups.
As reported earlier today, Motorola's second-quarter charge of $170 million to be taken against pretax earnings reflects the write-down of technology development costs and manufacturing equipment.
In the conference call, Motorola declined to give any guidance on second quarter earnings, which are expected to be released on July 8.
